Morning light arrives without asking permission, spilling through blinds in quiet golden stripes. It lands on the floor, on unfinished books, on yesterday's coffee mug, and reminds me the world turned while I slept. 

We spend so much energy trying to steer that turning. We make lists, five-year plans, elaborate maps for futures that rarely follow roads. I used to believe control was the same as care, that if I worried enough, prepared enough, I could prevent anything from breaking. 

Life taught me otherwise, gently. The ocean does not calm itself because you demand stillness. You learn to sail instead. You mend your sails, read the wind, bail water when needed, and keep going. Your job was never to command the sea, only to keep your small boat afloat. 

That realization feels like freedom. If I cannot control the waves, I can finally stop apologizing for them. I can focus on what is actually mine: how I speak to people I love, whether I notice beauty, whether I try again tomorrow. 

Lately I find comfort in smaller certainties. The hiss of the kettle. Ink bleeding into paper. A friend's unexpected message. Sun on my face. These moments do not need to be large to be meaningful; they only need to be noticed. 

And perhaps that is enough for today. Not solving everything. Not becoming someone new overnight. Just noticing light, sipping coffee slowly, and sailing onward with whatever wind I am given. Tomorrow will arrive in its own time anyway.
